Refs: FR-105, FR-110, NFR-101, dal-001, dal-002, dal-003, dal-004, adp-004, adp-006, scn-001, anom-008, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources, docs/qa.md section 30, docs/qa.md section 31.

Synthetic RF adapter. Input: scenario type, parameters, and seed from the scenario generator. Output: RF source records on a sensor x channel x time grid, each carrying sensor ID, sensor location, timestamp, channel index, channel centre frequency, band, power, SNR, bandwidth, signal type, and baseline delta, converted by the DAL into canonical RF observations. Constraints: fully determined by scenario type, parameters, and seed; emits no data of its own accord outside a scenario run; every sensor reports on every channel at every interval, so a missing reading is a detectable gap rather than an ambiguous absence; carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: two runs with identical type, parameters, and seed producing different RF observation sequences fails the spec. A second failure case: emitting a sparse grid in which a sensor silently omits channels it has nothing to report on, which makes a genuine dropout indistinguishable from a design choice. Amended 2026-09-11, before implementation, because this item is the body scn-003's batch executes and the decisions below are the ones that would otherwise be settled silently while writing it. Five of them. First, the module is app/adapters/synthetic_rf.py -- one module per source, beside opensky.py -- and it is a driver only: the stream is scn-001's emitter in app/scenario/emitter.py and stays there, so nothing that invents a number moves into the adapter layer. It mirrors replay_window's shape and takes its repository and pseudonymiser rather than constructing either, so the adapter/DAL seam RQ1 measures is the same seam on both sources rather than two different arrangements to compare a third against. Second, the unit of work is one run, not one window -- deliberately the opposite of adp-007's choice, and for a reason that only holds on this side: a synthetic run regenerates byte-identically from its seed, so all-or-nothing at run scale costs nothing to retry, whereas a replay that lost twelve committed batches would have to re-read the corpus. A run that fails part-way must therefore leave no observations at all, or scn-003's skipped run is a partial one that later counts as evidence. One run at the shipped layout is 5,040 records -- seven sensors x eight channels x ninety ten-second ticks over fifteen minutes -- comparable to one of adp-007's twelve replay batches, so the larger transaction that argument rejected does not arise here. Third, every observation this adapter produces carries data_mode SYNTHETIC, which is the field op-001's SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA badge reads; the badge is a property of the data rather than a UI constant, so a synthetic reading stored as replayed makes the interface lie about what the analyst is looking at. Fourth, the pseudonymiser is carried and unused: IDENTIFIER_RULES has no entry for RF, so substitute is a no-op on these payloads, and the argument is passed anyway rather than made optional at the DAL -- a single ingest entrypoint carrying a bypass for one source is no longer the architectural guarantee dal-002 and dal-003 rest on. Fifth, this adapter creates no scenario_runs row, records no ground truth and marks nothing complete. It is handed a scenario_run_id and writes observations under it; the run lifecycle belongs to the producer of the run, which is scn-003. Failure cases added by this amendment. A stored observation carrying data_mode replayed, or any value other than synthetic, fails the spec. A run whose stored observation count is not sensors x channels x ticks fails the spec, which is the dense-grid constraint above re-asserted against the database rather than against the in-memory stream -- a gap that only appears after persistence is invisible to every test scn-001 wrote. Observations surviving in the store from a run whose ingest raised part-way fails the spec, since the batch runner above would then skip a run that had already written half its grid. Accepted plus quarantined not equalling the number of records emitted fails the spec, which is dal-002's nothing-is-silently-dropped guarantee reduced to arithmetic at this level, as adp-007 reduces it at its own. Refs: FR-106, FR-108, FR-201, scn-001, scn-002, scn-003, scn-005, api-009, dal-001, dal-002, dal-003, dal-004, db-003, adp-007, op-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

Third source adapter, the extensibility measurement. Input: a simple additional source, for example a synthetic source-health feed. Output: canonical observations of a new observation type flowing through the unchanged DAL, plus a recorded measurement of files touched, lines changed, and hours taken. Constraints: the DAL, canonical model, and detection layer must require no modification beyond registering the adapter and its payload type; this is RQ1 evidence, not a feature, and is built late. Failure case: needing to alter the canonical observation model or a detection rule to accommodate the new source is a reportable negative result and fails the spec as written. Refs: FR-107, US-E2, US-R6, dal-001, docs/research_scope.md RQ1.

OpenSky corpus extraction and archive. Input: a locally downloaded raw OpenSky hourly state-vector file (states_YYYY-MM-DD-HH.csv.tar, wrapping one gzipped CSV member, from the anonymously readable data-samples bucket), a bounding box, and an output directory. Output: under data/opensky/ -- opensky_extract.parquet, the bounding-box-filtered Parquet extract, gitignored and never committed, plus a bounded sample of rows whose lat or lon is null, retained deliberately so the quarantine path has real input; manifest.json, committed, recording source URL, snapshot hour, download date, the licence and the required attribution text verbatim, the SHA-256 checksum of the original raw file, and a content checksum of the extract; and coverage.json, committed, the coverage report giving the per-icao24 inter-sample gap distribution against the 10-second cadence. Constraints: neither the raw file nor the extract may be committed, because the OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(iii) forbids making the data available to anyone outside the licensee's institute; reproducibility is carried instead by the committed manifest plus a fetch-and-filter entrypoint that re-downloads against the recorded checksum and re-filters, so a fresh clone reproduces the extract in one command once the reader accepts the same licence; download and filter are separate operations and the filter itself performs no network access, so it is testable offline against a small fixture; filtering is deterministic, so re-running against the same raw file and bounding box yields an extract with identical row content and column schema, verified against the recorded content checksum rather than by byte equality, since Parquet writers embed non-deterministic metadata; licence and attribution are captured at download time and stored verbatim, because the terms as published on that date cannot be reconstructed later; Parquet is the archive format for this extract alone and is never a read path for observations, which are served from PostGIS; the corpus lives under data/opensky/ rather than scenarios/, which is reserved for scenario fixtures -- this is replayed source data, not a fixture. A bounding-box test cannot be applied to a null coordinate, so a pure spatial filter would exclude every null-position row and leave dal-002's quarantine path exercised by fixtures alone and AC-02 undemonstrated on real data; the filter therefore also retains the first N rows with a null lat or lon in file order, N being configuration with its value and the resulting count recorded in the manifest. File order is used rather than a seeded sample so the retention needs no seed of its own and stays deterministic for a given raw file. Such a row can only ever reach quarantine, never a canonical observation, so retaining it adds evidence without any risk of contaminating the operational picture or a metric. The coverage report computes its gap distribution over positioned rows only, since a null-position row is not a coverage gap. Failure case: a filter step that downloads the snapshot itself when the raw file is absent fails the spec, because it reintroduces the network dependency the archive exists to remove and makes the filter untestable offline -- the same failure adp-001 guards against at replay time. A second failure case: opensky_extract.parquet or the raw file appearing in git fails the spec as a licence breach, and a manifest missing the original checksum, the licence, or the attribution text fails it because the artefact is then neither reproducible nor attributable. A third failure case: an extract containing no null-position rows at all, which silently removes the only real-data input dal-002 has and reduces AC-02 to a fixture claim. A fourth failure case: a coverage report whose natural gap distribution overlaps the gap durations the aircraft-coverage-gap scenario will inject must fail acceptance and force a different bounding box, never be waived, because genuine and injected dropouts would then be indistinguishable and the false-positive rate uninterpretable. Refs: FR-105, FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-601, AC-02, adp-001, scn-002, anom-008, docs/implementation.md Track 0, docs/qa.md section 21.

Fetch-and-verify entrypoint for the OpenSky corpus, the network half of the corpus tooling. Input: a source URL and expected SHA-256 read from the committed manifest, a destination directory, and an explicit licence acceptance. Output: the raw tarball downloaded to data/opensky/raw/ and verified against the recorded checksum, followed by the adp-004 filter, so one command takes a fresh clone to opensky_extract.parquet, manifest.json and coverage.json. Amended 2026-08-21: the command itself is adp-006. This item delivers the fetch-and-verify function; until adp-006 landed the one-command claim was met only by a multi-line python -c invocation, which is not a command. Constraints: this is the only module in the corpus tooling permitted to open a socket, which is what keeps the adp-004 filter network-free and testable offline; the checksum of the downloaded file is verified before the filter runs, not after, so a corrupted or substituted file never reaches the extract; the download writes to a temporary path and is moved into place only once verified, so an interrupted run leaves nothing that a later run would mistake for a complete file; a run whose destination already holds a file matching the recorded checksum skips the download rather than re-fetching roughly 180 MB; licence acceptance is an explicit act by the operator, not a default, and the licence and attribution are displayed at the point of acceptance, because the whole reason the extract is not committed is that acceptance belongs to the reader rather than being bypassed by handing them the bytes; every test mocks the transport and no test in the suite performs a real download. Failure case: a checksum mismatch that still produces an extract fails the spec, because the artefact would then be unattributable to the recorded source and the manifest would assert a provenance that does not hold; the run must abort and leave no extract, manifest or coverage report behind. A second failure case: a partially downloaded file left at the destination path, which a later run would accept as complete and filter into a silently truncated extract. A third failure case: downloading without explicit licence acceptance, which makes the tool take a licence action on the operator's behalf. A fourth failure case: any test performing a real network call, which makes the suite slow, non-deterministic, dependent on OpenSky's hosting, and quietly turns continuous integration into an unattended acceptor of someone else's terms. Refs: FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-601, AC-12, adp-001, adp-004, ops-003, docs/qa.md section 21, docs/implementation.md Track 0.

Command-line entrypoint for the corpus build, the operator surface over adp-004 and adp-005. Input: an invocation of python -m app.corpus.build carrying a data directory, an explicit licence-acceptance flag, an optional bounding-box override, an optional null-retention bound, and the pseudonymisation seed read from the environment, with backend/.env loaded by the entrypoint so the seed does not have to be exported by hand. Output: exit code 0 with opensky_extract.parquet, manifest.json and coverage.json written per adp-004, and a summary naming what was written, the row counts, the content checksum, and the seed fingerprint; a non-zero exit with a diagnostic naming the cause on every failure path. Constraints: this is the one command adp-005 promises, which until now was met by a multi-line python -c invocation -- not a command, not documentable in a README without inviting transcription error, and the vehicle for the download_date trap below. The bounding box defaults to the box recorded in the committed manifest rather than to a literal in code, so the manifest remains the single authority on what the corpus covers and a re-filter cannot silently apply a different box from the one that built the extract; an explicit flag overrides it, and overriding is what a deliberate box change looks like. download_date is derived rather than supplied: when adp-005 skips the download because the destination already matches the recorded checksum, the existing manifest's download_date is carried forward unchanged, and only an actual download records today's date. The recomputed content checksum is compared against the one already in the manifest before any artefact is overwritten, and a difference aborts the run with both values reported; proceeding requires an explicit flag, because replacing the corpus every recorded measurement was taken against is a deliberate act rather than a side effect of re-running a build. Licence acceptance is an explicit flag with no default and the notice is displayed before it is checked, per adp-005. The pseudonymisation seed is read from the environment and is never a command-line flag, because a flag is recorded in shell history and visible in process listings; a missing seed aborts before any file is written, per dal-004. Nothing derived from the seed other than its SHA-256 fingerprint is printed or written. Failure case: defaulting download_date to today on a run whose download was skipped, which writes a false provenance date into a committed artefact and is precisely the trap the manual invocation carried. A second failure case: overwriting the manifest when the recomputed content checksum differs from the recorded one, which silently replaces the corpus behind every measurement already taken and reported. A third failure case: a run that leaves a partial artefact set behind when a later step fails -- the manifest must not be rewritten unless the extract was written, the same all-or-nothing argument adp-005 makes for the download. A fourth failure case: exiting 0 on any of the above, since a command that reports success on failure cannot be used in a script or in CI. A fifth failure case: accepting the licence by default, or reading acceptance from an environment variable rather than from an explicit act by the operator. A sixth failure case: the seed appearing in a flag, in the summary output, or in the manifest, any of which discloses the key and makes every pseudonym reversible by exhaustive search over the icao24 space. Refs: FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-401, NFR-601, AC-12, adp-004, adp-005, dal-004, ops-003, docs/qa.md section 27, docs/qa.md section 28, docs/implementation.md Track 0.

Replay entrypoint, the operator surface over the adapter and the DAL. Input: an invocation of python -m app.replay carrying an optional window length in seconds, an optional start and end bounding the span replayed, and a data directory; DATABASE_URL and PSEUDONYM_SEED from the environment. Output: the archived extract driven through adp-001's reader, the DAL, and db-003's PostGIS repository into a live database; a scenario_runs row created for the replay; a summary on stdout reporting rows read, observations accepted, records quarantined, batches written, and wall time; a non-zero exit status when the replay fails. Also: a make replay target running it in a container, and PSEUDONYM_SEED passed through into the backend and pipeline compose services from the host environment as ${PSEUDONYM_SEED}, with no default of any kind. Amended 2026-09-04 during implementation: this item originally specified Compose's required form, ${PSEUDONYM_SEED:?}, so that an unset seed failed on the host. That was wrong. Compose interpolates the whole file for every command regardless of profile, so a required variable makes up, migrate, test and demo all demand a seed only replay needs -- and make demo on a clean machine is AC-12. Verified by running it: with the seed unset, docker compose config itself exits non-zero. The loud failure moved rather than being lost, to Pseudonymiser.from_environment, which raises before anything is written and names backend/.env.example. Constraints: this command constructs nothing the adapter should own -- replay_window already takes its repository and pseudonymiser, and this item supplies them. It calls init_engine() explicitly and disposes on exit, because db-005 made get_engine() refuse to build lazily and no FastAPI lifespan runs here. It loads .env, following app/corpus/build.py rather than app/main.py, so the two operator CLIs behave alike and main.py remains the single documented exception (docs/qa.md section 37). The seed is never committed and never defaulted (dal-004). Four decisions fixed 2026-09-04, before implementation, and recorded because each is a real constraint rather than a detail. First, this command creates its own scenario_runs row, with scenario_type 'replay-only', seed 0, empty parameters and null ground_truth: observations carries a NOT NULL foreign key to that table, no scenario generator exists yet, and a command requiring a run nothing can create would be unrunnable. scn-001 supersedes this, and the placeholder scenario_type is what makes such rows identifiable when it does. Second, the unit of work is one window, not one run -- so dal-002's all-or-nothing guarantee holds per batch and a run interrupted part-way leaves the windows already written in place. That is a deliberate weakening of what dal-002 promises at run scale and is stated here rather than discovered; a whole-hour single transaction was rejected as a 133,634-row write held open for the length of the replay. Third, it does not reuse the pipeline compose service, whose command points at app.pipeline, a module that does not exist -- make replay runs compose run --rm backend, mirroring migrate. Fourth, the summary exists to make the corpus figures reproducible: the wall time currently on record was taken with a throwaway script, measures the reader and the DAL against the in-memory fake rather than PostGIS, and is recorded inconsistently as 2.44 s in thesis_notes.md and 2.46 s in qa.md and the handoff. Re-taking it through this command and reconciling both documents is part of this item. Failure case: PSEUDONYM_SEED unset must fail before any row is written, and must not fall back to a default or to an empty seed -- a replay that silently pseudonymises under an empty seed produces a corpus whose identifiers cannot be reconciled with any other run. A second failure case: an unreachable database, a missing extract, or a window outside the corpus span must exit non-zero with a message naming which of the three failed; exiting zero over a replay that wrote nothing fails the spec. A third: a real icao24 or callsign reaching any persisted row fails the spec (dal-004). A fourth: the reported accepted and quarantined counts not summing to rows read fails the spec, because that is the arithmetic dal-002's nothing-is-silently-dropped guarantee reduces to at this level. Refs: FR-105, FR-104, NFR-101, US-E7, AC-02, AC-12, adp-001, adp-004, dal-002, dal-003, dal-004, db-003, db-005, ops-003, scn-001, docs/qa.md sections 37 and 39. Implemented 2026-09-04. Measured through this command against the full corpus, in containers, with the PostGIS repository: 133,634 rows read, 133,134 accepted, 500 quarantined, 12 batches of 300 simulated seconds, 14.25 s wall time -- against ~2.4 s for the same corpus through the in-memory fake, so persistence is about 5.8x the cost of reading and normalising. Cross-checks reproduced independently in the database: 30,276 observations with no altitude, 948 distinct aircraft, every geometry at SRID 4326, and zero rows mentioning icao24 or callsign. Two defects were found by running it and were unreachable from the test suite: DEFAULT_ENV_FILE was anchored to the repository root, which does not exist inside the container, and Compose passing an unset variable through as an empty string shadowed backend/.env because load_dotenv treats present-but-empty as present. Both now carry regression tests.

Injection-exclusion list for track perturbation. Input: the archived extract, the bounding box from the committed manifest, a minimum gap length, and the pseudonymisation seed. Output: data/opensky/natural_gaps.json, committed, naming every aircraft carrying a natural reporting gap while airborne and away from the box edges - identified by its DAL pseudonym rather than by icao24 - with each gap's start, end and duration, and the parameters the analysis ran under. Constraints: a gap counts only when it starts and ends inside the box with the aircraft airborne at both ends, because an aircraft leaving the box or parked on the ground produces an interval that is an artefact of the filter rather than a coverage failure; identifiers are pseudonyms so the artefact can be committed without carrying source identities (dal-004), and are therefore meaningful only against the seed whose fingerprint the manifest records; the analysis is deterministic and the artefact is regenerated by the same command that builds the corpus (adp-006). Failure case: reporting a gap distribution with no identifiers, which is what coverage.json already does and what leaves the exclusion unbuildable - the point of this item is the identity, not the duration. A second failure case: committing icao24 values, which would place source identities in the repository that dal-004 exists to keep out. A third failure case: counting a gap whose ends straddle the bounding box, which is the error the box sweep already made once and corrected. Refs: FR-202, adp-004, adp-006, dal-004, scn-002, anom-008, docs/thesis_notes.md.

Seeded reproducibility of scenario runs, landed with the smallest seeded emitter. Input: a scenario type, a parameter set, and an optional integer seed; the RF layout from scn-005; and a simulated start time and duration. Output: a run record carrying the type, the parameters and the seed actually used, and a stream of RF source records on the layout's sensor x channel x interval grid, one reading per cell, whose serialisation is byte-identical to that of any other run with the same three inputs. Constraints: no wall-clock time, no unseeded randomness and no process-dependent ordering may influence output, so each cell's values are derived from the seed and the cell's own coordinates - sensor, channel index, tick - rather than from the order draws are taken in, and derivation uses a stable digest rather than Python's per-process salted hash; the seed is always recorded, including when it was generated rather than supplied; the run row is written through the storage layer rather than by SQL in a command module, superseding adp-007's placeholder run row, and is marked complete per db-007. Scope: this item emits the unperturbed baseline only - injection is scn-002's and persistence through the DAL is adp-002's - and its records carry no scenario type and no ground truth, per api-009. Failure case: identical inputs producing different output, or differing seeds producing identical output, both fail the spec; the second is the trap, since a generator that ignores its seed entirely is trivially reproducible and useless. A second failure case: output that changes when PYTHONHASHSEED differs between two processes, a difference that is stable within a process and so survives every in-process test. A third failure case: a run whose seed was generated automatically rather than supplied and then not recorded, which can never be repeated. A fourth failure case: two runs with the same seed and different parameters producing identical output, since a parameter that controls nothing is the same defect as a seed that controls nothing. Refs: FR-201, US-E1, NFR-601, AC-01, api-006, api-009, scn-002, scn-003, scn-005, adp-002, adp-007, db-007.

The five scenario types. Input: one of normal-baseline, gnss-degradation, rf-sensor-fault, aircraft-coverage-gap, ambiguous-mixed-evidence, with parameters and a seed (scn-001). Output: the RF stream from scn-001's emitter with that type's injected component added per cell; for track-perturbing types, replayed track source records altered between the adapter and the DAL; and a ground-truth record written to scenario_runs.ground_truth at generation time, naming the type, the affected sensors, channels and aircraft, the simulated window, and the affected area. Signatures: normal-baseline injects nothing on either side; gnss-degradation raises the noise floor on the L1 channel alone or across all eight - spectral extent is a parameter, never a sixth type - and freezes the reported position of aircraft inside the affected area while their contact staleness stays fresh; rf-sensor-fault deviates one sensor while its spatial neighbours stay nominal, on a single channel or on all eight, since anom-007 must weight those differently; aircraft-coverage-gap suppresses replayed rows for chosen aircraft in a window; ambiguous-mixed-evidence stages a single-sensor RF deviation with a co-located contemporaneous coverage gap, so a sensor fault and genuine localised interference are both consistent with the evidence and the correct hypothesis is that they cannot be distinguished. Constraints: the injected component is a separately keyed derived quantity per cell, so adding it moves no baseline value a previous run produced (scn-001); ground truth is recorded at generation time, never inferred from detector output, and never leaves the run record (api-009); track perturbation sits between the adapter and the DAL rather than inside either, since adp-001 is specified as a pure reader and dal-003 owns provenance; aircraft chosen for any track-perturbing type exclude those carrying a natural interior airborne gap (adp-008), or a real dropout and an injected one become indistinguishable and the false-positive rate for that type is meaningless. Failure case: normal-baseline injecting any deviation at all fails the spec, because anom-008 and the false-positive rate depend on it being genuinely clean. A second failure case: adding a sixth scenario type for broadband interference rather than parameterising the existing one. A third failure case: an injected run whose readings differ from the same seed's normal-baseline run in cells the injection does not touch, which would mean the injection moved the noise rather than added to it. A fourth failure case: ground truth appearing on any observation, anomaly or API response for a scorable run. Refs: FR-202, FR-204, FR-108, AC-04, scn-001, scn-005, adp-001, adp-002, adp-008, anom-007, anom-008, api-009, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.2.

Batch execution. Input: a scenario type, a parameter distribution, a base seed, and a run count between 20 and 30. Output: N runs with distinct derived seeds, each with its own recorded parameters and ground truth, executed without manual intervention. Constraints: derived seeds are a deterministic function of the base seed, so the whole batch is reproducible from one value; a failing run is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the batch. Failure case: one run raising and terminating the batch, or two runs in a batch sharing a seed, fails the spec. Refs: FR-205, FR-1001, US-R2, scn-001, eval-001. Amended 2026-09-12, before tests, because the original text settles the loop and leaves every question about what one run of the loop does. Seven decisions. First, every run carries both halves: the synthetic RF grid through adp-002, and a window of the replayed corpus through adp-001 and the DAL under the same run id, with a TrackPerturber in front of it for the three types that stage on tracks. This is not confined to the track-perturbing types. rf-sensor-fault and normal-baseline stage nothing there and still need the stream present, because anom-005 fuses RF deviation with co-located track trouble and anom-006 fires on track trouble with a clean spectrum: in a run holding no tracks, 'no track trouble' is true by construction, so those rules stay silent for the wrong reason and the false-positive rate of the control measures the RF half alone. Second, per-run seeds are derived from the base seed by scn-001's keyed derivation rather than by advancing a sequence, so the batch is reproducible from one value and the derivation does not depend on how many runs preceded a given one. Measured 2026-09-12: thirty derived seeds from base 20220627 are all distinct and land on all seven layout receivers, between two and six runs each. Third, each run's simulated window is derived from that run's own seed and must lie inside the corpus span, because several runs in a batch necessarily share a zone centre -- there are seven centres and twenty to thirty runs -- and runs sharing both a centre and a window would be near-duplicates on the track side, differing only in invented noise. Fourth, the window and duration are written onto the run row with the parameters. RunSpec.as_parameters currently records the baseline and incident parameters and neither start nor duration_seconds, so scn-001's reproduction property holds in the test suite, where the window is a module constant, and not from the database. A batch claimed to be reproducible from one value whose rows cannot regenerate their own streams is not reproducible in the sense that matters. Fifth, the unit of work is deliberately one act per half rather than one per run, and this is a weakening stated here rather than discovered later: adp-002 commits a run's RF grid in a single act and the track window commits in its own, so a run that fails between the two leaves the first half behind. Nothing is deleted in response (db-007), the run is left with completed_at null, and every reader of runs filters on completion as api-006 already does. Making the whole run atomic would mean a third ingest path composing both sources into one call, bypassing both adp-002's entrypoint and adp-001's driver, which is a large structural cost to buy a guarantee the completion stamp already provides. Sixth, the batch reports per run: the derived seed, the type, accepted and quarantined counts for both halves, the number of aircraft actually staged, and whether the run completed. The staged-aircraft count is reported because detectability varies with it and the variation sits inside a batch: measured on the corpus over the default five-minute window, a 60 km zone holds 75 aircraft at Schiphol and 18 at Eindhoven, so the default 8% fraction stages about six aircraft in one and about one in the other, and aggregate recall over thirty runs would average a nearly undetectable run with an easy one and report a single number. Seventh, the operator surface is python -m app.pipeline, the module compose's pipeline service already names, taking a scenario type, a base seed, a run count and a data directory, with make generate passing a default through PIPELINE_ARGS as make replay passes REPLAY_ARGS; ops-003 is amended in the same change, since it currently records make generate as knowingly broken. It fails before it writes, as adp-007 does: a missing corpus, an out-of-range run count or a window outside the corpus span exits non-zero before an Engine is built. Failure cases added by this amendment. A run of any type whose observations contain no track records fails the spec, the quiet control included. A run row from which the run's stream cannot be regenerated -- no recorded window, or a recorded window that does not reproduce the stored readings -- fails the spec. A batch in which two runs share a derived seed, or in which every run shares one simulated window, fails the spec, the second because it makes runs sharing a zone centre near-duplicates on the track side. A failed run marked complete fails the spec, and so does a failed run that aborts the batch. A batch that reports only an aggregate and not a per-run outcome fails the spec, since a batch whose individual runs cannot be inspected cannot be reproduced selectively either. Known limitation, recorded rather than fixed: thirty fifteen-minute windows inside a single recorded hour overlap heavily, so track-side independence across a batch is bounded by the corpus rather than by the design. Refs additionally: adp-001, adp-002, adp-007, adp-008, db-007, api-006, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-008, ops-003, docs/qa.md sections 52 and 53.

Scenario Control screen. Input: the five scenario types and the recent-runs list from GET /api/v1/scenario/runs. Output: a scenario library, a run configuration form for parameters, seed, and batch count, run controls for start, pause, reset, and replay, a run status indicator, and a recent-runs table showing type, seed, and outcome. Constraints: the seed field is visible and editable, because this screen is the visible face of the evaluation harness; replay of a listed run reuses its exact recorded seed and parameters. Failure case: starting a run with no seed entered and no seed shown afterwards fails the spec, since the run would be unreproducible. Refs: FR-714, FR-201, US-E1, api-006, scn-001, nav-001. Amended 2026-09-13, before tests, because the original text names the screen's parts and settles none of the questions that decide what it may honestly claim. Eight decisions. First, the screen is built against the contract rather than the endpoint: api-006 does not exist, so a TypeScript contract file mirrors GET /api/v1/scenario/runs and POST /api/v1/scenario/start, a mock satisfies it, and the screen takes the value as a prop, exactly as operationalPicture.ts did before api-002 served it. A backend test parses that contract and compares field sets in both directions, as api-002's parity test does, so a field added on one side alone fails. This is not the case the phase-order amendment warns about: api-007's view filter and api-008's playback are server-side by specification, whereas everything this item is judged on -- the seed visible and editable, replay reusing a recorded run's seed and parameters, exactly five types, and the failure case below -- is client-side and provable today. The same seam was measured at Phase 5 at four files and 118 insertions with no data-consuming component changed. Second, the run controls render disabled, with the reason stated on screen, until a handler is supplied. A start button that posts nowhere claims a capability the system does not have; today a batch is started from the command line. Start, reset and replay are props; with none supplied the status indicator reads idle and the screen says why. Failure case: a control rendered enabled with nothing behind it fails the item, and so does hiding the controls rather than disabling them, since an unbuilt capability the screen conceals is the degradation NFR-204 requires to be visible. Third, the configuration form exposes exactly the dials the batch entrypoint accepts and no others: scenario type, base seed, run count between 20 and 30, per-run duration, and the five incident dials -- offset, duration, radius, elevation and spectral extent -- excluding --data-dir, which says where the corpus lives rather than what the run is. The design mockup shows noise amplitude, affected sensor count and gap duration; the generator accepts none of them, and a control that changes nothing is scn-001's fourth failure case in a different coat. Asserted by parity against app.pipeline's parser rather than by reading the form, so a dial added to either side alone fails. Fourth, the seed is rendered and edited as the decimal integer that is stored. The mockup shows 0xA4F2. A seed's only job is to reproduce a run -- pasted into PIPELINE_ARGS, or sent back by replay -- and a second representation is one more conversion to get wrong. Bounded by SEED_MAX, because a seed that does not round-trip through scenario_runs.seed cannot reproduce its run. Failure case: a seed rendered in a form the run record cannot hold. Fifth, the seed field may be left blank and the seed actually used comes back. The screen never invents one: scn-001 requires the seed to be recorded including when it was generated rather than supplied, and api-006 requires start to echo it. The item's stated failure case is restated as this -- a run started from this screen whose seed appears nowhere afterwards fails, whether because the field was blank or because the returned record was not rendered. Sixth, replay repopulates the configuration from the listed row rather than starting the form's current state under that row's seed, which would be reproducible in name only. RunSpec.from_record is the server-side half of the same guarantee and already refuses a row that cannot describe its own window. Failure case: replaying a run whose recorded parameters the screen silently drops. Seventh, pause is not built here and the divergence is recorded rather than left silent. FR-714 lists start, pause, reset and replay; FR-806 specifies start, reset and runs only, and generation has nothing to pause -- a batch is a loop of whole runs, each committing atomically in about three seconds, so the only coherent meaning is stop-after-the-current-run, a server-side lifecycle nothing specifies. Pause belongs to FR-717's playback transport over a recorded run's simulated time, which is op-008 on the Operational Picture. Revisit if api-006 gains a lifecycle. Eighth, the recent-runs table shows the scenario type and that is not an api-009 violation. api-009 forbids the answer key, and the type as a label, on observations, detector inputs, evidence bundles and the analyst-facing picture; this screen is the evaluation harness's own face and FR-714 requires the type on it. The table carries type, seed, start and an outcome derived from whether the run is marked complete (db-007), never the ground truth's contents, which ScenarioRunSummary has no field to hold. Scope: the screen, its contract and its mock. It adds no routing -- the screen becomes reachable when nav-001 lands -- and it does not implement api-006. Refs adds: api-009, db-007, scn-003, NFR-204, FR-717, op-008.

RF sensor and channel layout. Input: a layout configuration file, or the packaged default when none is given. Output: a validated layout of six to eight RF sensors at recorded geographic positions, each reporting on eight 2 MHz channels with centre frequencies 1567.42, 1569.42, 1571.42, 1573.42, 1575.42, 1577.42, 1579.42 and 1581.42 MHz, at a fixed interval of simulated time. Constraints: one channel is centred exactly on GNSS L1 at 1575.42 MHz, with four channels below it and three above, so frequency adjacency runs in both directions from L1; channel indices are contiguous from zero and centre frequencies strictly ascending, so adjacency by index is adjacency in frequency; sensor positions are discriminating at the layout's recorded radius, meaning every sensor has at least one other sensor within that radius and at least one beyond it, which is what makes the neighbour test in anom-007 non-vacuous and the spatial-coherence test in anom-005 non-trivial; the layout is configuration loaded and validated at run time, not hard-coded constants, so it can be varied without editing generator or detector code. Failure case: a layout with fewer than six sensors, or one in which some sensor has no other sensor beyond the radius - every sensor inside every plausible affected area - makes spatial clustering undiscriminating and must be rejected at load rather than accepted and detected later. A second failure case: a channel plan with no channel centred on L1, which removes the band the gnss-degradation scenario targets. A third failure case: silently accepting a malformed, incomplete or missing layout file, rather than failing loudly before any observation is generated. Refs: FR-108, FR-109, scn-002, adp-002, anom-002, anom-004, anom-005, anom-007, evb-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

Stage only on aircraft that are airborne in the run's window. Input: the corpus records a run replays, the staged zone from scn-002, and the run's window. Output: a target set containing only aircraft observed airborne inside the zone during the window, and a ground truth answer key naming exactly that set. Constraints: the airborne test is made where the targeting decision is made, not compensated for afterwards, following adp-008's precedent of keeping unsuitable tracks out of a run rather than correcting the metrics later; the target draw stays order-independent and derived from the run's seed, so a run remains reproducible per NFR-601; an aircraft airborne for part of the window and on the ground for the rest is eligible, because it is detectable for the part it was flying. Failure cases: an answer key naming an aircraft that is on the ground in every one of its reports fails the spec; a run whose eligible target set is empty must record that it staged nothing rather than staging on an ineligible aircraft; and a fix applied by filtering the answer key while still perturbing ineligible aircraft fails, because the perturbed records would remain in the run as unlabelled staged data. Written 2026-09-16, on measuring anom-011. The measurement that forces this item: across 77 staged runs of the three track-perturbing types, 381 aircraft were recorded as staged and only 172 were ever airborne -- 55 per cent of every injection lands on an aircraft parked for the whole run. The generator's zone test checks position against the radius and nothing else, so an aircraft parked at an airfield inside the zone is targeted like any other. anom-010 then refuses it correctly, because an aircraft on the ground stopped reporting when it was switched off and its stale position is indistinguishable from that. The consequence is that every parked target is a guaranteed false negative in eval-002's metrics for a reason that has nothing to do with detection quality. Measured effect on the recall figure: 25 per cent over all staged aircraft against 55 per cent over those that were airborne at any point, and for gnss-degradation 37 per cent against 74. The alternative considered and rejected was to keep the targeting as it is and exclude parked aircraft from the answer key instead. It produces the same recall arithmetic and leaves the perturbed records in the run, so a parked aircraft would carry a staged disruption that the ground truth does not mention -- unlabelled staged data in a corpus whose whole value is that its answer key is complete. A falsifiable prediction is recorded with this item and is the reason it is worth building before the fusion rules: anom-004 measured no separation between a staged run and its matched control at any radius from 5 to 60 km, and roughly doubling the detected staged findings per run may change that. It is to be re-measured after this item lands, and the result reported whichever way it falls. Refs: FR-304, FR-308, NFR-601, adp-008, anom-004, anom-008, anom-010, anom-011, eval-002, scn-002, scn-003.

RF threshold rule, rule ID RF-NOISE. Input: RF observations in a window and the baseline for the band from anom-002. Output: an anomaly of type rf_noise_deviation carrying severity, time window, affected area, and the observation IDs that triggered it. Constraints: the threshold is configuration, not a literal in the rule; the rule is deterministic, so the same observations always give the same anomaly. Failure case: observations at exactly the baseline must produce no anomaly, and observations one unit above threshold must produce exactly one. Refs: FR-301, FR-303, anom-002, evb-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, on picking it up after anom-002. Nine decisions. First, this item is a detector and not a writer: it takes readings and a baseline table and returns findings, touching no database, which is what lets it be tested without Docker and keeps FR-904's rule true one layer up. Persisting an anomaly needs its own item, and that item inherits a problem recorded here rather than discovered there -- the anomalies table's affected_area column is a NOT NULL polygon, and this rule produces no polygon, for the reason in the ninth decision. Second, the triggering readings are identified by their natural key -- sensor id, channel index, timestamp -- and not by a database id. CanonicalObservation has no id field at all, deliberately, and adding one would put storage identity on the model dal-001 keeps free of storage concepts. The natural key is unique because scn-005's grid is dense: every sensor reports every channel every interval, so the three values name exactly one reading. It is also the better artefact for this phase's purpose -- 'RF-03, channel 4, at 12:07:30' is a reference an analyst can check, and a bigint is not -- and evb-002 can resolve it against the database as readily as a surrogate id. Third, the comparison has a direction per metric and is not an absolute deviation. Raised power is the noise signature; falling SNR is the same event seen the other way round, because noise rising is what drives SNR down. An absolute deviation would report a channel quieter than baseline as noise, which is a different fault entirely and probably a dead receiver. Fourth, the threshold is an absolute offset from the baseline mean in the metric's own units, supplied as configuration. It is deliberately not a multiple of the baseline's standard deviation: that is anom-003, and keeping the two apart is what makes them independent evidence about the same reading rather than one detector counted twice in a bundle. Fifth, the comparison is strictly greater than, so a reading exactly at the threshold raises nothing. The item's existing failure case fixes the two ends and this fixes the boundary between them. Sixth, severity is Low, Medium or High and nothing else, per ui-001, derived from configured bands in the metric's units. The measured exceedance is carried on the anomaly for traceability and is never rendered as a score, which is the same arrangement anom-003 makes for its z value. Seventh, the unit of output is one anomaly per cell per contiguous episode of exceedance, not one per reading. A run emits 5,040 readings, so per-reading anomalies would produce thousands of findings describing one event, and evb-001's grouping would then be repairing damage this rule did rather than doing its own work. An episode carries its first and last exceeding reading as its window. Eighth, a cell whose baseline is insufficient is reported as unjudged rather than passed over in silence. This matters to anom-008 more than to this item: a detector that skips what it cannot measure would let 'zero anomalies on a clean run' be satisfied by not having looked, and the false-positive rate computed from that is meaningless. Ninth, the affected area of a single-sensor deviation is the sensor's own position, a point. An area requires corroboration from more than one sensor, which is anom-004's clustering and anom-005's fusion, and inventing a radius here would mean choosing a coverage footprint the project has never modelled. Following dal-001, no geometry type appears on the model: coordinates only. Failure cases added. A reading below its baseline by more than the threshold must raise no noise anomaly. A reading exactly at the threshold must raise nothing. A cell with no usable baseline must be reported unjudged and must not be counted clean. A run of consecutive exceeding readings in one cell must produce one anomaly and not one per reading. Refs adds: anom-008, ui-001, dal-001, scn-005, FR-904.

Rolling-average baseline engine. Input: observations from normal-baseline runs, a metric, and a window length. Output: a baseline value against which deviation is measured, computed per metric per sensor per channel for RF metrics and per metric per region for track metrics. Constraints: the baseline derives from normal-scenario data only; per-channel granularity is required so that a quiet channel and a noisy one on the same sensor are not averaged into a baseline that fits neither; a window with insufficient samples returns an explicit insufficient-data result, not a misleading average over one point. Failure case: computing a baseline from a window containing injected anomaly data, or returning a value from a single sample as if it were a baseline, fails the spec. A second failure case: pooling channels into one per-sensor baseline, which hides single-channel deviations inside the spread of the others. Refs: FR-302, FR-301, FR-108, anom-001, anom-003, anom-007, scn-002, scn-005. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, after the baseline data was measured rather than assumed. Against the twenty completed normal-baseline runs in the development database: 100,800 RF readings over 56 sensor-channel cells (seven sensors, eight channels), 1,800 samples per cell, cell means spanning 0.177 dB from -95.081 to -94.904 dBm, and per-cell standard deviations from 1.437 to 1.551 dB. The cells are statistically indistinguishable on quiet data, and that has a consequence this item must state rather than let a mutation pass discover: its second failure case -- pooling channels into one per-sensor baseline, hiding single-channel deviations inside the spread of the others -- cannot be demonstrated against baseline runs, because there is no between-channel variation for a pooled baseline to hide anything inside. An implementation replacing per-cell baselines with a pooled one would survive every test built from the quiet grid, which is the same defect shape as the api-010 tests that could not fail: a test distinguishing A from B must be built from values occurring in only one of them. The granularity is justified structurally, not empirically on clean data. It is what makes anom-007's single-channel-against-broadband discrimination possible once something is injected, and the cells are uniform only because scn-001's baseline emitter is uniform by construction. Added constraint: the test proving per-channel granularity is built from staged runs, or from a constructed series in which cells genuinely differ, never from normal-baseline data alone. Added failure case: a per-channel claim proved only against quiet runs fails the spec, because such a test cannot tell the implementation apart from the pooled one the item forbids. Refs adds: anom-007, scn-001, api-010. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, on starting to build it. Scope narrows to RF metrics. The item asks for a baseline per metric per region for track metrics as well, and that half is not built: no region concept exists anywhere in the project, and nothing consumes a track baseline -- anom-001, anom-003 and anom-007 all read RF baselines, and anom-010's staleness threshold is configuration by its own text rather than a deviation from an average. Building it would mean inventing a region definition to satisfy a signature nothing calls, and picking that definition badly before a consumer exists to judge it. The engine is therefore written per cell rather than per sensor-and-channel, with the RF cell being sensor id and channel index, so the track half is a second cell extractor plus a region decision rather than a rewrite. This is recorded as a narrowing rather than done silently; the track half needs its own item when something wants it. Three further decisions. First, the engine cannot tell for itself which runs are quiet, because an observation carries no scenario type at all -- api-009 forbids it, and dal-001 gives the model nowhere to put one. So the caller supplies the run ids the baseline may draw from and the engine refuses any observation from outside that set, which turns 'derives from normal-scenario data only' from a convention the caller is trusted to honour into this item's first failure case, enforced where it can be tested. Second, the window is a trailing duration evaluated at a point: observations outside [end - window, end] do not contribute, and the end defaults to the newest observation supplied. That is what makes it a rolling average rather than an average, and what makes 'a window with insufficient samples' a real state rather than a description of an empty input. Third, the sample standard deviation is carried on the baseline beside the mean and a zero one is flagged rather than hidden, because anom-003's own failure case is a degenerate baseline dividing by zero and it reads the baseline from here. Refs adds: anom-010, dal-001, api-009, FR-303.

Z-score deviation detector. Input: a metric series, its baseline mean and standard deviation from anom-002, and a z threshold. Output: anomalies for points whose absolute z-score exceeds the threshold, each carrying the computed z and the rule ID. Constraints: the z value is stored on the anomaly for traceability but is never rendered to the analyst as a score, per ui-001. Failure case: a series with zero standard deviation must not divide by zero; it returns no anomalies and records the degenerate baseline. Refs: FR-301, ui-001, anom-002, evb-002.

Spatial clustering of track discontinuities. Input: track-continuity anomalies in a time window and a cluster radius. Output: clusters of discontinuities with a representative centroid and affected-area geometry, computed by the PostGIS query in db-004. Constraints: clustering is spatial and deterministic; isolated discontinuities outside the radius form no cluster. Failure case: two discontinuities separated by more than the radius must not be reported as one cluster. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, db-004, anom-005. Amended 2026-09-15, before tests, on measuring the question this item was written to answer. Two defects corrected and two decisions forced by measurement. First defect: the clustering query is db-009 and not db-004. This item said 'computed by the PostGIS query in db-004', which is the proximity query FR-905 names and describes; db-001's comment on its GiST index repeats the same error. db-009 was written when db-004 was picked up and found to describe a different query. Second defect: this item's constraint that 'isolated discontinuities outside the radius form no cluster' contradicts db-009, which returns a lone finding as a group of one deliberately, because anom-006 must know that a dropout happened alone -- a source that goes quiet by itself is an infrastructure problem rather than an incident. The constraint is replaced: an isolated discontinuity forms a group of one, and it is the consuming rule that decides what a group of one means. First decision, and the one that changes this item's purpose: the output is an intermediate finding and cluster size is never on its own reportable. Measured 2026-09-15 over eight seed-matched triples from the stored batch, the largest cluster a staged run produces is identical to the largest cluster in its own matched control in all eight, at every radius from 5 to 20 km; at 30 to 60 km the difference is 0.12 to 0.25 clusters, with one or two triples of eight differing at all. Findings per run are 15.9 on staged runs against 16.0 on controls. The control is an rf-sensor-fault run at the same seed, not a normal-baseline run: no normal-baseline run in the batch shares a seed with a staged one, so it replays a different stretch of corpus and would confound the injection with the traffic, while rf-sensor-fault shares seeds and perturbs nothing on the track side -- its ground truth records zero staged aircraft against 2 to 11 in each matched staged run. Clustering track gaps alone therefore provably cannot distinguish a staged run from its own control, and a rule reporting on cluster size would be reporting background. Second decision: the radius is a parameter and is explicitly not fitted. The measurement covers 5 to 60 km and the separation is between zero and 0.25 clusters across all of it, so no value is chosen because it worked; the default is set to the scale of a staged incident, whose zone radius is 60 km, and this measurement is recorded beside it. A radius selected by searching for one that made a control go green would be fitted to eight triples of one batch. Failure cases added. A cluster radius of zero or less is refused rather than answered, per db-009. A rule raising a reportable anomaly on cluster size alone fails this spec. And the count of clusters on quiet runs is recorded alongside the reportable count, per anom-008's amendment, because it is the number that moves first if the corpus or the generator changes underneath the detectors. Refs adds: db-009, anom-008, anom-010, anom-011, eval-002.

Fusion rule, rule ID FUSION-SPATIAL. Input: RF noise anomalies from anom-001 and track-gap clusters from anom-004. Output: an anomaly of type possible_interference_zone when both occur in the same simulated time window and within the configured distance, carrying references to both contributing anomalies. Constraints: both conditions are necessary; the window and distance are configuration. Failure case: RF noise and track gaps in the same area but in non-overlapping time windows must not raise this anomaly, and neither must a co-occurrence with only one of the two present. Refs: FR-305, US-A2, db-004, anom-001, anom-004, evb-001.

Data-source issue rule, rule ID SOURCE-GAP. Input: track dropout clusters and the set of RF anomalies for the same window and area. Output: an anomaly of type possible_data_source_issue when dropouts are present and no co-located RF anomaly exists. Constraints: this rule is the discriminator that keeps a coverage gap from being reported as interference; it is mutually exclusive with anom-005 for the same cluster. Failure case: an aircraft-coverage-gap scenario producing possible_interference_zone instead of possible_data_source_issue fails the spec. Refs: FR-306, scn-002, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3.

Sensor fault rule, rule ID SENSOR-FAULT. Input: an RF sensor reporting abnormal readings, the readings of its spatial neighbours in the same window, and the readings of the frequency-adjacent channels on the sensor itself. Output: an anomaly of type possible_sensor_fault when the sensor is abnormal and its spatial neighbours are nominal, with the frequency-adjacency test recorded as a distinct piece of evidence rather than folded into the spatial one. Constraints: spatial neighbour selection is a spatial query with a configured radius, not a hard-coded sensor list; frequency neighbour selection is the adjacent channel indices on the same sensor. A real emission raises adjacent channels together, so an isolated single-channel deviation with clean neighbours is evidence about the sensor rather than the environment. Failure case: several adjacent sensors all reporting abnormal readings must not raise a sensor-fault anomaly, since that pattern indicates an environmental cause. A second failure case: a deviation spanning all eight channels on one sensor being reported with the same confidence as a single-channel one, since the broadband pattern is weaker evidence of a fault. Refs: FR-307, FR-108, scn-002, scn-005, db-004, anom-001, anom-002.

Correct non-detection on a normal-baseline run. Input: a completed normal-baseline scenario run with no injected deviation. Output: zero anomalies of any type. Constraints: this is a required positive behaviour of the detection engine, not an absence of behaviour; it is asserted for every detector, not only in aggregate. Failure case: any anomaly raised on a clean run fails the spec, because the false-positive rate reported in eval-002 becomes meaningless if the engine is noisy on clean data. Refs: FR-308, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, eval-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 14. Amended 2026-09-14, before any detector was written against it, on measuring the corpus. The constraint that a normal-baseline run produces zero anomalies of any type is scoped here to the reportable ones -- the fused rules an analyst is actually shown, being anom-005's possible_interference_zone, anom-006's possible_data_source_issue and anom-007's possible_sensor_fault. It does not count the intermediate findings those rules consume. The measurement that forces this: a quiet run contains roughly 138 aircraft, of about 530 seen, whose reported position staleness exceeds 100 s, and about 8 intervals between consecutive reports exceeding 100 s before filtering. Those are real properties of real replayed data, not defects in the detector and not artefacts of the pipeline, and a rule requiring the track detector to emit zero of them would be requiring it to be wrong. Read the other way, the unamended constraint would be satisfiable only by a detector that failed to notice genuine discontinuities in its input. The control's purpose is unchanged and is what the scoping protects: on a run with nothing staged, nothing reaches the analyst, and the false-positive rate in eval-002 is computed from that. Two obligations are added rather than dropped. The rate of intermediate findings on quiet runs is recorded alongside the reportable count, because it is the number that would move if the corpus or the generator changed underneath the detectors and nothing else would show it. And the assertion stays per detector rather than in aggregate, as this item already requires -- for an intermediate producer the assertion is that its findings are within the recorded background rather than that there are none. Failure cases amended. A reportable anomaly of any of the three fused types raised on a clean run still fails the spec, unchanged. A detector reporting zero intermediate findings on a quiet run now also fails it, because the corpus is known to contain them and silence means the detector did not look. Recorded as a threat to validity: this scoping makes the false-positive rate a statement about the fused layer only, and a reader could mistake it for a statement about detection as a whole. The evaluation reports both numbers for that reason. Refs adds: anom-010, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, dal-001.

Detection latency measurement. Input: an anomaly and its scenario run ground truth. Output: latency as the simulated-time delta between injected event onset and anomaly emission. Constraints: simulated scenario time only, never wall clock; the definition is fixed before any measurement code exists, per the Track 0 item in docs/implementation.md; the unit is recorded alongside the value. Failure case: a latency that changes when the same run is replayed on faster hardware fails the spec, because it proves wall-clock time leaked in. Refs: FR-309, FR-1002, NFR-601, scn-001, eval-002.

Track continuity rule, rule ID TRACK-GAP. Input: aircraft position observations for one scenario run, a staleness threshold, and the run's simulated time window. Output: a track_continuity_gap anomaly per affected aircraft, carrying the gap's onset and end in simulated time, its duration, the last known position as the anomaly's location, and the observation IDs either side of the gap. Constraints: staleness is the simulated-time interval between consecutive reports for one pseudonymised aircraft, never wall clock, consistent with anom-009; the threshold is configuration, not a literal in the rule; the rule is deterministic, so the same observations always give the same anomalies. Failure cases: an aircraft whose last report is the final one before the run window closes must raise nothing, since every track still in flight is stale at the end of every window and a rule that fires there fires on all of them at once; an aircraft that leaves the bounding box or lands must raise nothing, because ceasing to report is correct behaviour in both cases and neither is a discontinuity; and a gap one interval below threshold must raise nothing while one interval above raises exactly one. Refs: FR-304, FR-301, FR-306, adp-001, adp-004, anom-002, anom-004, anom-006, anom-008, db-004, scn-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3. Written 2026-09-14, on picking up Phase 8, because FR-304 had no spec item at all. Nine anom items covered eight of the nine detection requirements; anom-004 clusters track-continuity anomalies and anom-006 consumes track dropout clusters, and nothing in the backlog produced one. The rule the fusion pair is built on was the one rule nobody had written down. Two decisions. First, the unit is the gap rather than the aircraft: one anomaly per discontinuity, not one per stale track, because anom-004 clusters discontinuities by location and an aircraft with two gaps in different places is two pieces of spatial evidence rather than one. Second, and the reason this item cannot be written as a bare threshold: the corpus contains genuine dropouts, and normal-baseline replays the corpus. The coverage acceptance check of 2026-08-19 measured 10 of 948 tracks (1.05 per cent) carrying a genuine interior airborne dropout, with seven of the ten falling in the 100-300 s band that scenario type 4 injects into. A staleness rule over a normal-baseline run will therefore fire on real corpus gaps, and anom-008 requires that run to raise zero anomalies of any type. The conflict is settled here rather than discovered as a failing anom-008 test. Raising the threshold above 300 s is rejected: it would blind the detector to exactly the band the injected gaps occupy, buying a clean false-positive rate by disabling the measurement it is the control for. Relaxing anom-008 to anomalies attributable to injection is rejected: FR-308 makes correct non-detection a required behaviour, and a control that permits known firings is not a control. The accepted answer is the exclusion already owed by the Track 0 residue -- the generator refuses the ten identified tracks as corpus-window content, using the coverage report to identify them -- extended from injection sites, where it was owed, to baseline windows, where it is equally needed and was not previously noticed. Added failure case: a normal-baseline run raising a track_continuity_gap from a genuine corpus dropout fails this item as well as anom-008, because it means the exclusion was not applied. Recorded limitation: the exclusion removes real data to make a false-positive rate measurable, so the reported rate is conditional on it, and the measured rate with and without the exclusion is owed to the evaluation. Amended 2026-09-14, before tests, after measuring the corpus rather than reasoning about it. The corpus-dropout decision written into this item that morning was wrong by about two orders of magnitude and is corrected here rather than quietly replaced. It assumed the ten tracks adp-008 names were the whole false-positive problem. Measured across the twenty normal-baseline runs in the development database, the background is this: of roughly 530 aircraft seen per run, 137.7 reach a peak reported position staleness above 100 s, 19.3 above 300 s, and 1.0 above 600 s. The equivalent gnss-degradation figures are 141.1, 20.7 and 0.6 -- so the staged signature is about 3.4 aircraft per run against a background of 137.7, and above 600 s the quiet runs are higher than the staged ones. No threshold separates them at any value. The cause is not a tuning error: the injection stages disruptions of 100-300 s because that is what a plausible real coverage failure looks like, and it is also what a real one is, so the staged effect was designed into the densest part of the distribution it has to be told apart from. Five decisions follow. First, this item's output is an intermediate finding and not a reportable anomaly. It is computed for anom-004 to cluster and is never shown to an analyst, for the reason anom-008 is amended alongside: a quiet run genuinely contains of the order of 138 track discontinuities that are real properties of real data, so a control requiring zero of them would require the detector to be wrong. What the rule detects is staleness; what it cannot do is attribute it, and attribution is spatial and cross-modal by design -- the background gaps are scattered across 309,000 square kilometres while a staged one sits inside a zone about 20 km across with a raised noise floor over it. Second, there are two detection mechanisms because the two scenario types stage differently, and a rule with only one of them is blind to one type. gnss-degradation rewrites the reported position staleness and the rows keep arriving; aircraft-coverage-gap suppresses the rows entirely, so nothing arrives to read a field from. The rule therefore reports a frozen_position finding from a reading whose position staleness exceeds the threshold, and a not_heard finding from an interval between consecutive reports of one aircraft that exceeds it. The shape is carried on the finding, because it is exactly what anom-005 and anom-006 need to tell interference from a data-source failure. Third, the frozen_position mechanism additionally requires contact to be fresh, and this is a measured decision rather than a tidy one. Requiring fresh contact alongside stale position -- the two-clock discriminator dal-001 documents -- narrows the quiet-run background from 137.7 aircraft per run to 24.6 while leaving the staged margin unchanged at 3.4, so the signal-to-background ratio improves from about one in forty to about one in seven. It is the single largest improvement available to this rule and it costs nothing. Fourth, two filters apply, and they are the same two the bounding-box sweep and adp-008 both needed. An aircraft on the ground is excluded from both mechanisms, because a parked aircraft stops reporting for the uninteresting reason that it has been switched off. A not_heard finding additionally requires both ends of the gap to lie inside the corpus bounding box by a margin, because an aircraft that flies out of the box and back leaves an interval with nothing in it and nothing went wrong; the interior test does not apply to frozen_position, which has no gap to bracket. Measured on the quiet runs: 164 intervals exceed 100 s, 32 survive the airborne filter, 23 survive both, and those 23 belong to four aircraft every one of which is on the adp-008 list, with none unlisted. Omitting the two filters would mean four-fifths of the findings were artefacts of having drawn a box and of aircraft being switched off. Fifth, the exclusion list stays the generator's responsibility and is not duplicated here. The measurement above is an independent validation of adp-008 from a different code path -- built at corpus-build time from raw archive rows, checked here against pseudonymised observations in PostGIS after a full replay -- and it also confirms the list is not being applied to baseline windows, which is owed work on the generator rather than a defence to add to the detector. Failure cases added. A reading whose position is stale but whose contact is equally stale must not raise a frozen_position finding, because that shape is an aircraft not being heard from rather than one reporting a frozen position. A gap whose either end lies outside the bounding-box margin must raise no not_heard finding. A gap either of whose ends has the aircraft on the ground must raise nothing. The superseded failure case about a normal-baseline run raising a track_continuity_gap no longer applies and is withdrawn: a quiet run raises many, by design, and anom-008 is amended to say what the control actually counts. Refs adds: adp-008, dal-001, anom-005, anom-006.

Track-gap detection sensitivity, and the recall figure the fusion rules depend on. Input: the stored scenario runs with their ground truth, and the TRACK-GAP rule from anom-010. Output: a per-aircraft recall figure for each staged scenario type, measured against the answer key rather than against a control, together with an account of where the undetected staged aircraft are lost -- the perturber's choice of which records to touch, the rule's airborne filter, its interior-to-box filter, or the requirement for a bracketing report either side of an absence. Constraints: measured on at least two independently seeded batches before any figure is reported as a property of the detector, because the figures here come from one; the answer key is the ground truth recorded at generation time by scn-002, never derived from the detector's own output; the investigation changes no detector behaviour by itself, so any fix it motivates is a separate item with its own tests. Failure cases: a recall figure quoted without the batch and policy it was measured under fails the spec, per the project's rule that a measurement without its conditions is a memory; and an account that attributes the loss without measuring it -- naming a filter as the cause rather than counting what each filter removes -- fails it too. Written 2026-09-15, on measuring anom-004 before writing it. The measurement that forces this item: across the seed-matched runs, 119 aircraft were actually staged on and 25 produced a finding, a recall of 21 per cent, 19 per cent for aircraft-coverage-gap and 25 per cent for gnss-degradation. The shapes are correctly assigned in every case, frozen_position for the degradation runs and not_heard for the coverage gaps, so the two-mechanism design of anom-010 is wired correctly and this is a sensitivity result rather than a wiring one. It is also not a tuning artefact: sweeping the staleness threshold across 60, 100, 150 and 200 s and the contact-freshness discriminator across 10, 30, 60 and 90 s and disabled entirely leaves recall flat at 19 to 26 per cent throughout. The injected disruption is 300 s beginning 120 s into the window, comfortably above every threshold tried, so the loss is not the threshold. This gates anom-005, anom-006 and anom-007. Measured across the twenty rf-sensor-fault runs, whose truth is a broken sensor and which stage nothing on the track side, a background track cluster lies within the fusion radius of the faulty sensor on 70 per cent of them at 60 km and 75 per cent at 85.7 km -- so anom-005 as specified would report possible_interference_zone on most of the runs whose correct answer is possible_sensor_fault, and anom-006 being mutually exclusive with it for the same cluster means the false fusion removes the run from the rule that would have been right. Requiring three or more members in a cluster cuts that exposure from 70 to 25 per cent and cannot be used, because at 21 per cent recall a staged run yields one to three findings in total and only one measured run produced three detections on staged aircraft: the threshold that suppresses the background suppresses the signal, because they are the same size. The conclusion is one number rather than three problems -- the background is not too large, the recall is too small -- and the fusion rules must not be built until it is understood, or three items will pass their unit tests on constructed fixtures and fail together at evaluation time with the cause two layers below where the failure appeared. One interaction found on the way and not to be fixed by weakening anom-010: the aircraft-coverage-gap runs produce fewer findings than their own controls, because suppressing rows can remove the reports that would have bracketed a natural gap, and anom-010's refusal to extrapolate a gap from a track's final report is correct and stays. Refs: FR-304, FR-305, FR-306, FR-308, anom-004, anom-005, anom-006, anom-007, anom-008, anom-010, scn-002, adp-008, eval-002, docs/phase8_detection.md.

Evidence bundle builder. Input: a group of related anomalies from one scenario run, grouped on three axes: simulated time window, spatial proximity, and frequency adjacency. Output: a bundle containing anomaly_type, time_window, affected_area, affected_channels, data_mode, an evidence list where each item has source, finding, and rule_id, and a known_uncertainties list. Constraints: this bundle is the only input the AI layer ever receives; raw observations never reach a model; anomalies on adjacent channels of the same sensor within the same window group into one bundle rather than several; the bundle carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: an evidence item lacking a rule_id, or a bundle built with an empty evidence list, fails the spec. A second failure case: a broadband event spanning eight channels producing eight single-channel bundles, which fragments one finding into eight and hands the AI layer an incoherent picture. Refs: FR-401, FR-402, FR-404, FR-108, US-R1, AC-05, ai-003, api-009, scn-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.4.

Evidence traceability. Input: a candidate evidence bundle. Output: a built bundle in which every evidence item resolves to a stored anomaly or observation ID. Constraints: resolution is checked at build time against the database, not asserted by the builder; the resolved IDs are persisted with the bundle so the grounding check in ai-008 has something to verify against. Failure case: a bundle containing an item whose rule_id or source reference matches no stored record must raise and must not persist a partial bundle. Refs: FR-403, US-R1, AC-05, evb-001, ai-008.

Hypothesis output schema. Input: a candidate hypothesis object from any generator. Output: a validated Pydantic model with hypothesis_title, confidence, summary, supporting_evidence, evidence_against_or_uncertainty, alternative_explanations, and recommended_human_action. Constraints: confidence is an enum of exactly Low, Medium, High; all fields are required; the same schema serves all three generators and is the source from which the hosted JSON schema and the local grammar are derived. Failure case: a hypothesis with confidence 87% or 0.87 must be unrepresentable, and one with a missing alternative_explanations field must fail validation rather than defaulting to empty. Refs: FR-501, FR-715, NFR-203, ui-001, ai-002, ai-004, ai-005.

Template hypothesis generator. Input: an evidence bundle. Output: a schema-valid hypothesis assembled deterministically from the bundle contents, with no model call. Constraints: no network, no API key, no model server; it is both the correctness fallback for ai-007 and the comparison baseline for the evaluation, so it must be usable in both roles; every supporting-evidence item it emits is copied from the bundle and is therefore grounded by construction. Failure case: the template generator emitting a claim absent from the bundle fails the spec and would invalidate the baseline. Refs: FR-502, US-R1, ai-001, ai-007, eval-004, docs/implementation.md Phase 9.

Provider-agnostic hypothesis service interface. Input: an evidence bundle plus configuration naming the provider, model ID, and generation parameters. Output: a validated hypothesis. Constraints: the interface is defined before either model provider is written, so no provider's request or response shape leaks into it; adding a provider touches one adapter module and configuration, nothing else; this doubles as a second data point for the RQ1 extensibility claim.
